ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a small-signal equivalent circuit. The drain node of the right-side transistor M2 is connected to the upper AC ground through resistor R_D, and this drain node is labeled v_out to the right. The feedback resistor R_F is connected from this right-side v_out node back to the lower-left input/source node of M1; this node is exactly the position where the small-signal input current source i_in is injected. The gate of M1 is grounded, and the drain of M1 then drives the gate of M2. Then reason: The problem statement indicates that i_in is the input current, and R_F is very large. Since R_F samples from the output node v_out, and its resistance is very large, it mainly slightly samples the output voltage, rather than sampling the output current in series at the output terminal. The feedback signal returns through R_F to the same node where the input current is injected, mixing with the input current at the input terminal in parallel/current form. Therefore the output sampled quantity is voltage, and the input mixed quantity is current, so the feedback type is voltage-current feedback.
